raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

On SM120/SM121, DeepSeek-V4.1 writes the V4 KV record and decodes it with FlashInfer's V4 sparse MLA kernels, and `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4_ds_mla` is rejected. FlashInfer's SM120 sparse MLA also decodes V4.1's own records (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5197). This PR writes the V4.1 record on SM120 and lets the KV cache option select the matching FlashInfer kernel. It is the base for further SM120 DSv4.1 work.

**Depends on FlashInfer ≥ 0.7.1:** the `fp8_dsv41` / `fp8_dsv41_fp4_ca` formats are in 0.7.1rc2 but not in the pinned 0.7.0.post1, so this needs the FlashInfer pin bump before it merges.

## Claims

- `fp8_ds_mla` on SM120 writes the 528 B V4.1 record (all 512 dims MXFP8) instead of the 584 B V4 record, and decodes it with FlashInfer's `fp8_dsv41` kernels: +8.7% KV tokens at TP4.
- `nvfp4_ds_mla` works on SM120 (previously rejected): MXFP8 sliding window plus an NVFP4 compressed cache, decoded with `fp8_dsv41_fp4_ca`: +31% KV tokens over `fp8_ds_mla`.
- GSM8K accuracy and fixed 8K/1K serving throughput are unchanged.

## Validation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4 on 4× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), FlashInfer built from main with #5197, one run per configuration.

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype {fp8,nvfp4_ds_mla} --block-size 128 --max-model-len 65536 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

| KV cache | FlashInfer format | KV tokens | GSM8K (chat, flexible-extract) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fp8` before this PR (V4 record) | `fp8` | 214,991 | 0.951 |
| `fp8` → `fp8_ds_mla` (V4.1 record) | `fp8_dsv41` | 233,679 | 0.945 |
| `nvfp4_ds_mla` | `fp8_dsv41_fp4_ca` | 305,319 | 0.948 |

GSM8K: lm-eval `gsm8k` through the chat template, 1,319 problems, 32 in flight, `max_tokens` 16384. The three scores are within one-run noise (±8 problems).

Fixed 8K input / 1K output (random prompts, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, 8 requests per concurrency), output tok/s; each pair ran at the same time on the two GPU halves of one host:

| Concurrency | V4 record (before) | `fp8_ds_mla` | | `fp8_ds_mla` | `nvfp4_ds_mla` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 105.7 | 105.6 | | 106.9 | 104.7 |
| 2 | 180.8 | 178.5 | | 183.3 | 179.8 |
| 4 | 314.9 | 315.7 | | 313.4 | 314.3 |
| 8 | 502.4 | 504.6 | | 505.2 | 502.0 |
| 16 | 732.1 | 734.2 | | 734.3 | 732.9 |
| 32 | 857.2 | 856.4 | | 859.0 | 1003.1 |
| 64 | 1039.7 | 1041.2 | | 1042.2 | 1036.4 |

All within 2%, except `nvfp4_ds_mla` at 32 in flight (+17%, one run, not yet explained and not claimed). No preemptions in any case.

Tests:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py   # 12 passed
pytest tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py \
  tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py    # 357 passed, 19 skipped (SM120)
```

The new unit tests run without a GPU. CI has no SM120 runner for the serving path; it was validated as above.

<details>
<summary>Validation environment</summary>

The serving runs used vLLM `e6674262f1` with this branch merged, alongside unrelated changes for other models. On the test host's kernel (which caps a single long-term pin below 2 GiB), the CPU-offloaded Engram tables also needed chunked pinning, a host-specific workaround outside this PR.
</details>

## Details

- **Record:** `_use_v41_mxfp8_kv_record()` now also returns true on the SM120 family, so the SWA and compressed caches, the indexer page alignment and DSpark all use the V4.1 record there, as on SM100. Its writers (the fused qnorm/RoPE/KV insert and the compressor insert) already handle it on every arch.
- **Kernel selection:** the SM120 layer passes `kv_cache_format` per call from the caches it reads: `fp8_dsv41_fp4_ca` when an `nvfp4_ds_mla` call includes the compressed cache, `fp8_dsv41` otherwise (FlashInfer has no `fp8_dsv41_fp4_ca` kernel without the compressed cache, which the uncompressed layers hit), and `fp8` for the V4 record.
- **Backend:** `DeepseekV4FlashInferMLASparseBackend` accepts `nvfp4_ds_mla` on SM120 only; the SM100 TRTLLM-gen kernels behind the same backend cannot read the NVFP4 compressed cache.
- **No version gate:** the KV cache option alone selects the kernel; older FlashInfer builds without the V4.1 formats are not supported on this path.
- **Related:** #57523 makes the same record switch for gfx950 (a small textual conflict either way). #57292, #56509 and #57028 change SM120 page geometry and are orthogonal. #59342 adds `nvfp4_ds_mla` to the V3.2 `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` backend on SM10x, a different backend and model.
- **Not a duplicate:** searched open and merged PRs for `fp8_dsv41`, `fp8_dsv41_fp4_ca`, `nvfp4_ds_mla SM120`, `DSv4.1 SM120`, `V4.1 KV record`, `mxfp8 kv record` and FlashInfer DSv4.1 sparse MLA; none switches SM120 to the V4.1 records or wires FlashInfer's V4.1 formats.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. (Claude Code wrote the change and this description; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and evaluations above.)

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.

- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

Third-party validation of the same capability, on a different SKU/TP shape: **8x RTX 6000D 84G (SM120 workstation), TP8+EP8, k7 probabilistic/block DSpark, vLLM `0.32.1rc1.dev463`** — plus one FlashInfer-version data point that may help unblock the pin discussion.

**End-to-end result (nvfp4_ds_mla vs fp8_ds_mla, same boots otherwise):**

| | fp8 | nvfp4_ds_mla |
|---|---|---|
| KV pool | 8,529,675 tok (8.13x @ 1M) | **13,290,418 tok (12.67x @ 1M, +55.8%)** |
| out tok/s (c1 / c8 / c32 / 64K-in-1K-out c8) | 128.9 / 533.9 / 948.6 / 165.1 | 131.7 / 439.7 / 983.1 / 162.4 |
| temp=0 determinism | distinct=1 | distinct=1 (reader mechanically correct) |
| fp8-path regression after patching | — | none (footer path bit-identical in our A/B) |

Quality profile: long-form clean, concurrency band identical to fp8; one trivial arithmetic prompt (`12*12=`) flips to a deterministic wrong answer under nvfp4 — consistent with 4-bit compressed-cache loss (we plan a GSM8K gate to quantify; the author's "GSM8K unchanged" may well hold there).

**The FlashInfer version data point:** on the stock `0.7.2.post1` wheel (pre-#6616), the SM120 reader only takes footer-scale pages, so the vLLM-side capability probe correctly refuses nvfp4_ds_mla rather than decoding garbage. We bridged it locally with kacper-daftcode/vLLM-Moet's 19-file `kv_scale_placement` patch (AOT-built; footer path verified bit-identical) — credit to them, patch lineage [here](https://github.com/kacper-daftcode/vLLM-Moet/tree/main/tools/dsv41_sm120/flashinfer_interleaved). With flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6616 merged (2026-10-18, native inline-scale records), that bridge should no longer be needed once vLLM pins a FlashInfer that contains it — which supports this PR's stated pin-bump dependency rather than complicating it.

Happy to re-run the validation leg against the PR head + a post-#6616 FlashInfer nightly if that helps the review.

Backport datapoint that may be useful for the pin discussion — and one detail that matters for anyone trying to run this PR before the FlashInfer bump lands.

**Environment:** 8× RTX PRO 6000 Max-Q 97.9 GB (SM120, **no NVLink**), TP8, `vllm 0.31.1rc1.dev253+g7d0b4e57a`, `flashinfer-python 0.7.2.post1`, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (NVFP4 MoE), DSpark k=3 (probabilistic/block), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`.

**Result: both arms fail at engine init in ~75 s on dev253.**

Applying the PR head to dev253: `nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py` and `utils/flashinfer.py` apply cleanly (offsets −8/−9, one hunk with fuzz 1); `deepseek_v41/attention.py` has one failing hunk that is comment-context only — the functional change (`_use_v41_mxfp8_kv_record()` returning True for SM120) aligns fine by hand.

Both `fp8` and `nvfp4_ds_mla` then die with the same first cause:

```
vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py:672
RuntimeError: DeepSeek-V4.1 on SM120 reads its inline KV records through
FlashInfer's 'fp8_dsv41_inline' cache formats; the installed FlashInfer does not provide them.
```

i.e. `has_flashinfer_sparse_mla_dsv41_inline()` is False. Probe detail on the stock 0.7.2.post1 wheel:

```
inspect.signature(trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4).parameters['kv_cache_format'].annotation
  -> Literal['fp8', 'nvfp4', 'fp8_dsv41', 'fp8_dsv41_fp4_ca']   # no *_inline variant
```

This matches @xzwgit's pre-#6616 note: the wheel only has the footer-scale formats.

**The part that may be worth flagging in the PR description / review:** on this base it is all-or-nothing, not "nvfp4 only". The `fp8` arm never asks for `nvfp4_ds_mla`, but once `_use_v41_mxfp8_kv_record()` returns True on SM120, `kv_mxfp8` becomes True, which trips the same inline-format probe. So a backport onto an older vLLM gives no partial win to measure — it refuses to start either way.

**Kernel side is already there**, which supports this being purely a pin issue:

```
flashinfer.mla._sparse_mla_sm120._DECODE_DSV4_DISPATCH contains
  (64, 512) (64, 1024) (64, 2048)  -> True on 0.7.2.post1
```

So the SM120 DSv4 decode specializations exist in the published wheel; only the inline-scale format enum is missing (merged in flashinfer#6616 on 2026-10-18, three days after 0.7.2 shipped on 2026-10-15).

Nothing to change on our side — the blocker is exactly the stated FlashInfer dependency. We have a ready harness (8-sample decode medians + 20-prompt exact-match quality gate + corruption probe) and will re-run both arms the day a wheel containing #6616 is published, then report back here.

+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize(

+        ("fp8_ds_mla", False, True, "fp8"),

+def test_inline_rows_skip_other_layers_pages_in_packed_blocks():
+    # Block size 4 packed with two other layers' pages: 12 rows per block.
+    slots = torch.tensor([[0, 3, 4, 9, -1]], dtype=torch.int32)
+    rows = dsv41_flashinfer._slots_to_inline_rows(slots, 4, 12)
+    assert rows.tolist() == [[0, 3, 12, 25, -1]]
+    assert rows.dtype == slots.dtype
+
+
+def test_inline_rows_are_slots_without_packing():
+    slots = torch.tensor([0, 5, -1], dtype=torch.int32)
+    assert dsv41_flashinfer._slots_to_inline_rows(slots, 64, 64) is slots
+
+
+def test_swa_inline_rows_are_mapped_once_per_step():
+    metadata = SimpleNamespace(block_size=4, flashinfer_sparse_index_cache={})
+    slots = torch.tensor([[0, 3, 4, 9, -1]], dtype=torch.int32)
+    lens = torch.tensor([4], dtype=torch.int32)
+
+    rows = dsv41_flashinfer._swa_inline_rows(metadata, "decode", slots, lens, 12)
+    assert rows.tolist() == [[0, 3, 12, 25, -1]]
+    # Later layers of the step reuse the first layer's rows.
+    again = dsv41_flashinfer._swa_inline_rows(metadata, "decode", slots, lens, 12)
+    assert again is rows
+    # A rebuild clears the cache, so new indices are mapped again.
+    metadata.flashinfer_sparse_index_cache.clear()
+    fresh = dsv41_flashinfer._swa_inline_rows(metadata, "decode", slots, lens, 12)
+    assert fresh is not rows and torch.equal(fresh, rows)
+    # Without packing the indices are already rows.
+    unpacked = dsv41_flashinfer._swa_inline_rows(metadata, "prefill", slots, lens, 4)
+    assert unpacked is slots
+

+def _sm120_kv_cache_format(
+    kv_cache_dtype: str, kv_mxfp8: bool, has_compressed_cache: bool
+) -> str:
+    """FlashInfer's SM120 sparse MLA format for the caches one call reads.
+
+    vLLM writes V4.1 MXFP8 records inline (each token's scales follow its own
+    data, as FlashMLA does), which FlashInfer reads as ``fp8_dsv41_inline``.
+    ``nvfp4_ds_mla`` keeps that record for the sliding window and stores the
+    compressed cache as inline V4.1 NVFP4 records, so a call that also reads the
+    compressed cache is ``fp8_dsv41_inline_fp4_ca``. Anything else is the V4
+    record (``fp8``).
+    """
+    if kv_cache_dtype == "nvfp4_ds_mla" and has_compressed_cache:
+        return "fp8_dsv41_inline_fp4_ca"
+    if kv_mxfp8:
+        return "fp8_dsv41_inline"
+    return "fp8"

+def _slots_to_inline_rows(
+    indices: torch.Tensor, block_size: int, block_span: int
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Map paged slot IDs to rows of the whole cache.
+
+    FlashInfer addresses inline V4.1 records as rows of the cache, so a block
+    that packs several layers' pages (``block_span > block_size``) shifts each
+    slot by the rows of the other layers before it. ``-1`` stays ``-1``.
+    """
+    if block_span == block_size:
+        return indices
+    blocks = torch.div(indices, block_size, rounding_mode="floor")
+    rows = indices + blocks * (block_span - block_size)
+    return torch.where(indices >= 0, rows, indices)
+

+
+    Every layer of a step reads the same SWA indices, so the first layer maps
+    them and caches the rows on the step metadata (cleared by each build).
+    """
+    if block_span == swa_metadata.block_size:
+        return indices
+    key = f"swa_rows_{phase}_{block_span}"
+    cached = swa_metadata.flashinfer_sparse_index_cache.get(key)
+    if cached is None:

+        swa_metadata.flashinfer_sparse_index_cache[key] = (rows, lens)
+        return rows
+    return cached[0]

Third-party validation of the same capability, on a different SKU/TP shape: **8x RTX 6000D 84G (SM120 workstation), TP8+EP8, k7 probabilistic/block DSpark, vLLM `0.32.1rc1.dev463`** — plus one FlashInfer-version data point that may help unblock the pin discussion.

**End-to-end result (nvfp4_ds_mla vs fp8_ds_mla, same boots otherwise):**

| | fp8 | nvfp4_ds_mla |
|---|---|---|
| KV pool | 8,529,675 tok (8.13x @ 1M) | **13,290,418 tok (12.67x @ 1M, +55.8%)** |
| out tok/s (c1 / c8 / c32 / 64K-in-1K-out c8) | 128.9 / 533.9 / 948.6 / 165.1 | 131.7 / 439.7 / 983.1 / 162.4 |
| temp=0 determinism | distinct=1 | distinct=1 (reader mechanically correct) |
| fp8-path regression after patching | — | none (footer path bit-identical in our A/B) |

Quality profile: long-form clean, concurrency band identical to fp8; one trivial arithmetic prompt (`12*12=`) flips to a deterministic wrong answer under nvfp4 — consistent with 4-bit compressed-cache loss (we plan a GSM8K gate to quantify; the author's "GSM8K unchanged" may well hold there).

**The FlashInfer version data point:** on the stock `0.7.2.post1` wheel (pre-#6616), the SM120 reader only takes footer-scale pages, so the vLLM-side capability probe correctly refuses nvfp4_ds_mla rather than decoding garbage. We bridged it locally with kacper-daftcode/vLLM-Moet's 19-file `kv_scale_placement` patch (AOT-built; footer path verified bit-identical) — credit to them, patch lineage [here](https://github.com/kacper-daftcode/vLLM-Moet/tree/main/tools/dsv41_sm120/flashinfer_interleaved). With flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6616 merged (2026-10-18, native inline-scale records), that bridge should no longer be needed once vLLM pins a FlashInfer that contains it — which supports this PR's stated pin-bump dependency rather than complicating it.

Happy to re-run the validation leg against the PR head + a post-#6616 FlashInfer nightly if that helps the review.

Backport datapoint that may be useful for the pin discussion — and one detail that matters for anyone trying to run this PR before the FlashInfer bump lands.

**Environment:** 8× RTX PRO 6000 Max-Q 97.9 GB (SM120, **no NVLink**), TP8, `vllm 0.31.1rc1.dev253+g7d0b4e57a`, `flashinfer-python 0.7.2.post1`, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (NVFP4 MoE), DSpark k=3 (probabilistic/block), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`.

**Result: both arms fail at engine init in ~75 s on dev253.**

Applying the PR head to dev253: `nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py` and `utils/flashinfer.py` apply cleanly (offsets −8/−9, one hunk with fuzz 1); `deepseek_v41/attention.py` has one failing hunk that is comment-context only — the functional change (`_use_v41_mxfp8_kv_record()` returning True for SM120) aligns fine by hand.

Both `fp8` and `nvfp4_ds_mla` then die with the same first cause:

```
vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py:672
RuntimeError: DeepSeek-V4.1 on SM120 reads its inline KV records through
FlashInfer's 'fp8_dsv41_inline' cache formats; the installed FlashInfer does not provide them.
```

i.e. `has_flashinfer_sparse_mla_dsv41_inline()` is False. Probe detail on the stock 0.7.2.post1 wheel:

```
inspect.signature(trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4).parameters['kv_cache_format'].annotation
  -> Literal['fp8', 'nvfp4', 'fp8_dsv41', 'fp8_dsv41_fp4_ca']   # no *_inline variant
```

This matches @xzwgit's pre-#6616 note: the wheel only has the footer-scale formats.

**The part that may be worth flagging in the PR description / review:** on this base it is all-or-nothing, not "nvfp4 only". The `fp8` arm never asks for `nvfp4_ds_mla`, but once `_use_v41_mxfp8_kv_record()` returns True on SM120, `kv_mxfp8` becomes True, which trips the same inline-format probe. So a backport onto an older vLLM gives no partial win to measure — it refuses to start either way.

**Kernel side is already there**, which supports this being purely a pin issue:

```
flashinfer.mla._sparse_mla_sm120._DECODE_DSV4_DISPATCH contains
  (64, 512) (64, 1024) (64, 2048)  -> True on 0.7.2.post1
```

So the SM120 DSv4 decode specializations exist in the published wheel; only the inline-scale format enum is missing (merged in flashinfer#6616 on 2026-10-18, three days after 0.7.2 shipped on 2026-10-15).

Nothing to change on our side — the blocker is exactly the stated FlashInfer dependency. We have a ready harness (8-sample decode medians + 20-prompt exact-match quality gate + corruption probe) and will re-run both arms the day a wheel containing #6616 is published, then report back here.
